entities.evidence: בְּאֶרֶץ שִׁנְעָר locates the plain in Shinar, the same land in which Genesis 10:10 locates Babel.

review.translation: [And it happened|0] [as they migrated|1] [from the east|2], [that they found|3] [a plain|4] [in the land of|5] [Shinar|6] [and settled|7] [there|8].

analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי introduces an event. בְּנָסְעָם מִקֶּדֶם gives its setting (“as they journeyed from the east”), and וַיִּמְצְאוּ בִקְעָה states what happened (“they found a plain”).
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ precedes the Qal wayyiqtol form יְהִי, third person masculine singular, used impersonally.

analysis.evidence: מִקֶּדֶם gives the point of departure. Their setting out provides the setting for וַיִּמְצְאוּ בִקְעָה, “they found a plain.”
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ introduces a temporal clause. The Qal infinitive construct of נָסַע takes a third-person masculine plural suffix as its subject.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 66328:4, 66056:5.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun with prefixed preposition מִן. The נ assimilates to the following ק, marked by the dagesh.

analysis.evidence: The travelers come upon בִקְעָה, a plain, in the land of Shinar and settle there. The verse describes an encounter during their journey and gives no indication of a search.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine plural. Its subject is the travelers.

analysis.evidence: בִקְעָה is the object of וַיִּמְצְאוּ ‘they found’. The phrase בְּאֶרֶץ שִׁנְעָר locates the plain in the land of Shinar, where the travelers settled.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the absolute state. The initial ב belongs to the noun.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68106:7, 66576:5.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ means “in.” The noun אֶרֶץ is of common gender and stands in the singular construct before שִׁנְעָר.

draft.change: Add a place-name entry for Shinar under its own consonants. The source gloss “ewe” and proposed root שנס lack support here.
draft.definition: Shinar is the land in which Genesis 10:10 locates Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh.
draft.evidence: The phrase בְּאֶרֶץ שִׁנְעָר identifies the region containing the four cities.

analysis.evidence: בִקְעָה בְּאֶרֶץ שִׁנְעָר means “a plain in the land of Shinar.” שִׁנְעָר names the land where the travelers found the plain and settled.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix. It follows the construct noun אֶרֶץ.
analysis.sense: The land containing Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh.

analysis.evidence: After the travelers find a plain in the land of Shinar, שָׁם (“there”) identifies that plain as the place where they settled.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol verb in the third person masculine plural.
analysis.sense: to take up residence in a place

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 66060:4, 66059:10, 66056:7.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected adverb of place with no prefix or suffix.
